message.content:
You are helping reimplement a closed program, `bimcraft-cli` 0.10.0 (the command line of a BIM modeler written in Rust; README at /workspace/README.md), as a new Rust program built only from observed behaviour. Several agents work in parallel, each owning one area. I own the EDIT area (`src/edit/`) and delegate to you the commands `purge`, `delete_type`, `rename_type` and `match_properties`.

## Hard rules (violating any fails the whole project)
- The original binary is `/workspace/executable` (execute-only). Use it only by running it (args, stdin, files, env). NEVER decompile, disassemble, hexdump, strace/ltrace or read it; never modify or delete it; NEVER run `./compile.sh`.
- No internet; don't look for the program's source anywhere. Rust standard library only.
- Edit ONLY `src/edit/purge.rs`, `src/edit/types.rs`, `src/edit/matchprops.rs` (you may add files `src/edit/library_*.rs` with their `pub mod` lines in `src/edit/mod.rs`, and add your commands to `always_step` there). Nothing else in the repo. Scratch scripts (Python is fine) live OUTSIDE the repo, in `/tmp/edit-library/`. Commit only Rust.
- The sandbox refuses shell commands it can't verify (loops, heredocs, `cd` outside the worktree, `$(...)` feeding python): write Python scripts to files in /tmp and run them as `python3 /tmp/edit-library/x.py`.

## Setup
You are in a git worktree. First make sure your HEAD contains commit 89ee1af ("Editing: module skeleton"): `git log --oneline -3`; if not, `git merge --no-edit worktree-agent-a76b15059404997b3`. Build with `cargo build --release` (about 15 s).

## The codebase (read the relevant parts first)
- `src/json.rs`: `Value` (insertion-ordered `Map`, `insert_sorted`), serde_json-identical float formatting (`1000.0`), `to_compact`/`to_pretty`, `.sorted()` (replies are printed sorted by main.rs: just return the Value), `jobj!{}`.
- `src/project.rs`: `Project` = `doc` (top-level sections in file order: `types` {category: {name: def}}, `materials`, `images`, `families`, `parameters`, `view_filters`, `view_templates`, `line_styles`… ; `insert_top`, `section_mut`, `remove_top`) + `elements` (each a JSON object; a wall's `type` is its type's GUID, a component's `family`/`type` GUIDs, a view's template, a layer's material…) + `library: BTreeMap<u64, Value>` (`{kind, name, guid}`: kinds `type:wall`, `material`, `picture`, `family`, `family-type`, `family-parameter`, `view-filter`, `view-template`…; `lib_find`, `lib_guid`, `lib_name`, `lib_find_guid`). Key order matters (files are compared byte for byte after normalising GUIDs): remove entries without disturbing the rest.
- `src/session.rs`: `Session::execute` resolves the command, snapshots, runs, runs `crate::check::check`, rolls back on error, records an undo step labelled by the catalog label when the project changed (seen: `purge {"dry_run": true}` makes no step; `delete_type`/`rename_type` make `Delete Type`/`Rename Type` steps — check whether one that changes nothing still does; `match_properties` → `Match Properties`).
- `src/commands/params.rs` (param readers with the original's texts), `src/edit/common.rs` (`ids_param` — `ids`, else `id`, with the original's errors —, `resolve`), `src/styles/` (done by another agent: line styles/patterns, fill patterns, region types, text and dimension types, parameters, phasing — reuse e.g. `styles::common` helpers and see how they rename/delete their own library entries), `src/media/` (materials, pictures: done).
- Other areas are being written in parallel and are empty stubs now: ARCH, STRUCTURE (`type`, `family`, `component` commands), VIEWS, READERS. Don't implement their commands; your commands must work on project files made by the ORIGINAL.

## How to test
Build input projects with the original: `/workspace/executable run --script s.txt --save in.bimcraft` (walls of several types, doors, windows, components of several families, `type {...}` to make types, `family {...}`, `material {...}` with pictures (`material {"name": "M", "texture": {"path": "x.png"}}`), `filter {...}`, `template {...}`, `graphics {"template": …}`; `/workspace/executable commands` lists every command and its parameters). A fixture with one element of most categories is `/tmp/edit-agent/fx/all.bimcraft` (`python3 /tmp/edit-agent/dump.py file [ids|categories]` dumps elements). `/tmp/edit-agent/lib.py` has `run(cmds, src=file, files=[...], exe=...)` → (code, replies, stderr, project dict) and `/tmp/edit-agent/probe.py in.bimcraft 'purge {}'` prints the reply and the diff (elements, top-level sections, library); use them, don't edit files under /tmp/edit-agent. To compare with yours: `MINE=<your worktree>/target/release/bimcraft-cli python3 /tmp/tools/cmp.py -f in.bimcraft -- run in.bimcraft --cmd 'purge {}' --save out.bimcraft` prints SAME or the diff. The hidden tests do this kind of comparison on many inputs: replies, error texts, saved files and undo labels must match exactly.

## Your commands (specs from `/workspace/executable commands`)
- `purge` (PU, Purge Unused): "{kinds?: [type|family|material|picture|filter|template, …], dry_run?} takes out what nothing uses, again for what that leaves unused: types and families unless `kinds` says; a category keeps a type and a family a type; with `dry_run` it lists what would go and changes nothing". Seen on a new project: `{"count": 63, "dry_run": false, "removed": [{"kind": "beam type", "name": "Beam 150 x 400"}, …, {"kind": "family", "name": "Air Terminal"}, …]}`. Work out what counts as a use for each kind (elements, other types' layers, families' forms and parameters, materials' textures → pictures, views' graphics → filters, views → templates, paint, schedules, favorites?…), the cascade ("again for what that leaves unused"), the order of `removed`, what goes from the library and the sections (and empty sections), errors for bad `kinds`.
- `delete_type`: "{category?: wall|floor|door|window|column|roof|ceiling|railing|…, family?, type?} deletes a type of a category (`category` and `type`), a family (`family`) or one of a family's types (`family` and `type`), as Revit's Delete on one in the Project Browser does; refused while an element uses it (it says how many), and for the last type of a category or of a family". Seen: `{}` → `delete_type: give `category` and `type`, or `family`, or `family` and `type``; ok → `{"deleted": {"kind": "wall type", "name": "Exterior - 300mm"}}`.
- `rename_type`: "{category?, family?, type, name} renames a type of a category (`category` and `type`) or one of a family's types (`family` and `type`) to `name`, as Rename in Type Properties does: the elements of it, and what else names it, follow, and it keeps its GUID; refused for a name another type of it has. Text types and filled region types rename with `rename` on `text_type` and `filled_region_type`". Seen: `{}` → `rename_type: `name` is required: the type's new name`; `{"ids": []}` → `rename_type: `ids` isn't one of its parameters: category, family, type, name`; ok → `{"renamed": {"from": "Exterior - 300mm", "kind": "wall type", "to": "X"}}`.
- `match_properties` (MA): "{from: id, ids: [id,…]} gives the elements in `ids` the type of `from` (and, for components, its family), as Revit's Match Properties does; only elements of `from`'s category take it, the rest come back in `skipped`. Returns {modified, skipped}". Seen: `{}` → `match_properties: `from` (an element id or GUID) is required`.
For each: every error and the order of checks (category names as typed: plural, case, `structural column`…; unknown type names and the lists they give), what changes in sections, library and elements, undo steps.

## Finish
Commit on your worktree branch (message ending with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Final message: your branch name and commit; per command what matches (tested with cmp.py) and what doesn't; what other areas must provide.

systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

Schedules: the fields chosen, project parameters and calculated ones among them, totalled.Schedule Properties: fields, filters, sorting and grouping, as Revit's tabs have them.

Pipe tool: two clicks, or a chain; centred on its height by default, falling or rising with a second height.Pipe type: its diameter (or width and depth, if it isn't round) and its material.
Section: a pipe is cut in poché along the line, across it in a ring.
Device tool: the Type Selector lists only the families of its kind; Space turns what you place.Cable tray type: a width by a depth, or round, in a material.
Plumbing: the starter fixtures, a pipe falling to a drain and a riser, in 3D with the walls hidden.Electrical: a tray, a board, luminaires and devices at their mounting heights.
Lightning Protection (SPDA): NBR 5419's vocabulary on the same runs and fixtures; Revit has no such tab.SPDA in 3D: terminals, down conductors and the earthing ring and rods.
Data tab: outlets, a rack, a patch panel and cabling, in NBR 14565's words.Data in 3D: a tray, cables dropping to their outlets, a rack.

380:| Filled regions | Annotate > Filled Region (FR) and Masking Region start a boundary sketch. Edit Type opens Type Properties for a selected region or the current sketch: duplicate and rename types; choose foreground and background patterns and colors separately; set masking; check the combined preview. A pattern's … button opens the patterns, to create and edit them. Apply/OK save the draft as one undo step; Cancel drops unapplied work. A type change updates every region using it; the palette's Type Selector controls the instance's type. Non-masking fills keep cut foreground patterns and projected model lines visible; masking fills cover the model. Sketches snap to visible model edges, detail lines, existing region boundaries and their own geometry, with the configured snaps and angle guides. |
401:| Views | The Project Browser opens floor plans, ceiling plans, elevations, sections, the 3D view and schedules in tabs; View > Close Inactive closes the others. Its tabs keep it to Views, Schedules, Sheets or Families (Legends are still to come), and its search narrows it as you type, marking what matched: each word must match an entry or a group it's in (`ceiling 2`), `*` stands for any run of characters and `?` for any one. View > Duplicate View (DP) makes a plan view of the plan on screen, plain, with detailing or as a dependent; so does a right click on a plan in the Project Browser, where a plan view also has Delete, and a plan view's name, view range and crop are in Properties as a level's are. The Project Browser's Families lists each system category's types (walls, floors, doors…) and the project's component families; a right click on a type or a family has Delete, which the project refuses while something uses it. Manage > Link Model (LK) links another project, and the Project Browser lists the linked models. Manage > Purge Unused (PU) lists what nothing uses, by kind (types and families checked, as Revit's), and takes it out in one undo step. A right click in any view opens a menu of what it and the selection can do: Cancel, Edit Type, Select All Instances, Delete, Hide Element, Hide Category, Override Graphics, Zoom to Fit, Zoom In, Zoom Out, and in 3D Home View |
522:| `delete_type` | | `category` and `type`, or `family`, or `family` and `type`: deletes a type of a category, a family, or one of a family's types; refused while an element uses it (it says how many) and for the last type of a category or of a family |
523:| `rename_type` | | `category` and `type`, or `family` and `type`, and `name`: renames a type of a category or one of a family's types; what's of it and what names it follow, and it keeps its GUID; refused for a name another type of it has |
524:| `purge` | PU | `kinds?` (`type`, `family`, `material`, `picture`, `filter`, `template`; types and families by default), `dry_run?`: takes out what nothing uses, again for what that frees; a category keeps a type and a family a type; `dry_run` lists what would go |

content.content:
An agent's own side can ask the same: `bimcraft-cli mcp --connect --read-only`, or `bimcraft-cli mcp --read-only house.bimcraft`
for a headless server that opens the file and then only reads it.

## Commands

| Command | Shortcut | Parameters |
|---|---|---|
| `autosave` | | `path`: atomically write a native recovery snapshot without changing the project path or undo history |
| `recover` | | `path`, `project?`: validate and open a recovery snapshot; later Save targets `project`, or asks for Save As without it |
| `wall` | WA | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `top_offset?` (mm above `top_level`, negative below it), `height?`, `base_offset?`, `arc?` (degrees each turns, counter-clockwise), `location?` (`centre`, `core-centre`, `exterior-finish`, `interior-finish`, `exterior-core`, `interior-core`), `attach_top?`, `attach_base?` (a roof or a floor), `room_bounding?` (false: rooms run past it, as Revit's Room Bounding off; `modify` turns it on and off) |
| `door` | DR | `at`, or `wall` and `offset?`; `type?`, `family?` (a door family's `type`, its first by default), `mark?`, `flip_facing?`, `flip_hand?` |
| `window` | WN | as `door`, plus `sill?` (a family's `Sill Height` by default) |
| `sketch` | | `lines` ([[[x, y], [x, y]], …]; an arc [[x, y], [x, y], [x, y]], its ends then a point it passes through): solves a sketch without making anything, the loops it closes into (outlines and their holes) and their area, or every problem with the lines it's about: ends no other line meets, lines that intersect or overlap (a line that crosses itself too), three or more lines at a point. A sketch is solved as the straight pieces its lines are drawn with (an arc or a circle is cut into chords): past 200,000 of them it is refused at once |
| `edit_boundary` | | `id` (a floor, a ceiling, a roof by footprint or a shaft), `sketch?`: its outline and holes redrawn as one sketch, a line sent back with its `id` keeping it; without `sketch`, the lines it has now, each with its id once it has one |
| `floor` | | `boundary?` (else the walls of the level) or `sketch?` (lines, in any order, solved into its outline and openings), `openings?` (holes in it, inside it and apart; over the walls, by default each loop of them standing free inside, joined to none of the outer ones and with no room in it), `level?`, `type?`, `offset?` (its top above the level), `slope?` (degrees) and `arrow?` (its tail and head: it rises from the tail toward the head), `structural?` (a floor that carries load, as Revit's Floor: Structural). An outline, and each opening, is simple: no edge across another or along it, none ending part way along one, no spike or keyhole slit (`ceiling`, `roof`, `shaft`, `modify`, `move` and `edit_boundary` hold to it too, saying which edges); a saved file that has one still opens. Its model pattern starts at `pattern_origin` and turns by `pattern_angle` (set with `modify`) |
| `ceiling` | | `point` (in a room: out to its walls' faces, open round the walls standing free inside it), `boundary` or `sketch`, `openings?` (holes in it, inside it and apart), `level?`, `type?`, `offset?` (its underside above the level, 2600) |
| `shaft` | | `boundary` or `sketch`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `height?`, `base_offset?`: a hole through the floors, ceilings and roofs on its way |
| `room` | RM | `point`, `name?`, `number?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `limit_offset?`, `base_offset?`, `frozen?` (keeps its boundary: it isn't found from the walls again) |
| `room_separator` | | `points` [[x, y], …], `level?`, `closed?`: room separation lines, one per segment, that bound rooms where there is no wall (an open plan) and nothing else |
| `column` | CL | `at`, `type?`, `angle?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `height?`, `base_offset?` |
| `structural_column` | CL | as `column`, in its own category and types |
| `reinforcement_preset` | | `name?`, `kind?` (beam, column, footing, floor), `params?` (what `reinforce` takes, but the host), `rename?`, `delete?`: a named set of parameters, kept in the project; no `name` lists them |
| `voltage` | | `name?`, `nominal?` (volts), `min?`, `max?` (the band a device may read within; 10 per cent either way unless given), `rename?`, `delete?`: a voltage of the electrical settings; one a distribution system supplies cannot be deleted; no `name` lists them |
| `distribution_system` | | `name?`, `phases?` (1, 2, 3), `wires?` (the line conductors and the neutral), `l_l?`, `l_n?`, `l_g?` (names of voltages; "" takes one away), `ground?` (TN-S, TN-C, TN-C-S, TT, IT), `rename?`, `delete?`: a distribution system of the electrical settings; a voltage the project lacks is refused; no `name` lists them |
| `wire_type` | | `name?`, `material?` (copper, aluminium), `temperature?` (°C), `insulation?`, `note?`, `sizes?` (`[{section, ampacity, label?}]`, mm² and amperes, which replaces the table), `rename?`, `delete?`: a wire type of the electrical settings; no `name` lists them |
| `reinforce` | | `host` (a beam, a column, a footing or a floor) or `hosts` (a list), `preset?`, `cover?`, `grade?`, `grade_stirrup?`, `clearance?`, and by host: `bottom`, `top`, `stirrup`, `skin`, `anchor` (beam), `bars`, `stirrup`, `ties`, `anchor` (column), `mesh` (footing), `bottom`, `top` (floor), `check?`, `aggressiveness?`, `fck?`: bars by rules, as `rebar` elements on layers, and notes from the check |
| `footing` | FI | `at`, `type?`, `thickness?` (400), `offset?` (its top over the level, 0), `angle?`, `level?`: an isolated footing |
| `beam` | BM | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `offset?` (the height of its `justify` line over the level at its start, 0), `end_offset?` (at its end, for one segment: it slopes), `justify?` (`top`, `centre`, `bottom`), `system?`: a beam for each segment |
| `pipe` | PI | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `offset?` (the height of its `justify` line over the level at its start, 0), `end_offset?` (at its end, for one segment: it falls or rises, or stands if the two points are one), `justify?` (`centre` by default), `system?`: a pipe for each segment |
| `conduit` | CN | as `pipe`: a conduit (eletroduto) for each segment, round |
| `cable_tray` | CT | as `pipe`, its type a `width` across by a `depth` deep: a cable tray (eletrocalha) for each segment |
| `wire` | EW | as `pipe`: a wire (condutor) for each segment, round; its `system` the circuit |
| `down_conductor` | DC | as `pipe`: a down conductor (condutor de descida) for each segment; the same point twice and two heights stand it upright |
| `ground_conductor` | GC | as `pipe`: an earthing conductor (the ring or mesh), usually under the level (a negative `offset`) |
| `cabling` | CB | as `pipe`: structured cabling for each segment, round; its `system` the link or the network |
| `strip_footing` | FW | `points`, `closed?`, `type?`, `level?`, `offset?` (its top over the level, 0), `system?`: a footing under a wall for each segment |
| `stair` | | `start`, `end?` or `angle?` (the way it climbs), `level?`, `top_level?`, `height?`, `width?`, `riser?` (the most each riser may rise), `tread?`, `landings?` ([{`at`, `turn`}]: after `at` risers, the next run going on (0), turned left or right (90, -90), or back beside it (180, -180)), `railings?` |
| `ramp` | | `start`, `end?` or `angle?`, `level?`, `top_level?`, `height?`, `width?`, `slope?` (percent, 8.33), `landings?` (`at` mm up), `railings?` |
| `railing` | | `host` (a stair or a ramp) and `side?` (`left` or `right`; both by default), or `path`, `level?`, `base_offset?`; `type?` |
| `roof` | | `level?` (the one above the lowest), `offset?`, `boundary?` (else the walls of the level below) or `sketch?` (its outline and courtyards), `courtyards?` (holes in it with eaves of their own, inside it and apart; over the walls, by default each loop of them standing free inside, joined to none of the outer ones and with no room in it), `overhang?`, `slope?` (0 is flat), `slopes?` (a slope in degrees for each edge, numbered as `gables` are, 0 for the roof's `slope`), `gables?` (edges left upright, edge i from point i to the next, a courtyard's numbered on after the boundary's), `gable?` (a rectangle's short ends), `extrusion?` (`line`, `profile` of `[along, up]` points, `from?`, `to`: swept across to the line's left), `openings?`, `join?` (a roof it ends against), `type?` |
| `dormer` | | `host` (a roof), `at` (on its slope: the front wall's middle), `width?`, `height?` (over the roof at the front), `slope?`, `window?` (a window type), `type?` (its walls') |
| `dimension` | DI | `refs` (each `{id, face?, point?}`: a wall's `centre`, `left` or `right` face, `start` or `end`; a door's or window's `centre`, or its jamb at the `start` or `end` side; a grid's line; with `point: start|end` that line's end; or a point on one, or `{endpoint: [x, y]}`), `at`, `level?`, `kind?` (`aligned`, `linear` with `orient?` horizontal or vertical, `angular` between two lines that meet, `radial` and `diameter` on what is round, `arc_length` along a curved wall or an arc), `type?`, `prefix?`, `suffix?`, `above?`, `below?`, `replace?`, `equality?` |
| `dimension_constraint` | | `id`, `equal?`, `locked?: [segment, …]`: keep an aligned or linear dimension's segments equal (EQ) or locked at their lengths; what it measures to then moves with what a command moves, or the command is refused |
| `dimension_text` | | `id`, `segment?`, `prefix?`, `suffix?`, `above?`, `below?`, `replace?`: a dimension's text, or with `segment` (0 west to east, as `labels` lists them) one segment's own |
| `dimension_type` | | `name?`, `like?`, `rename?`, `delete?` and Revit's type parameters (`string`, `tick`, `tick_size`, `line_pen`, `tick_pen`, `color`, `line_extension`, `witness`, `witness_length`, `witness_gap`, `witness_extension`, `baseline_spacing`, `centre_mark`, `font`, `text_size`, `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `width_factor`, `text_offset`, `background`, `read`, `units`, `decimals`, `radius_symbol`, `diameter_symbol`, `equality_text`): create, edit, rename or delete a dimension type; without `name`, lists them |
| `tag` | TG | `ids?` (without them, every door and window on the level not tagged yet, or of `category`), `label?` (the field it shows: any of its category's schedule fields), `level?`, `category?`, `offset?`, `leader?` |
| `text` | TX | `text`, `at` (its top left), `view?` (a level's plan by default; a section, an elevation, or a sheet by number), `size?` (mm on paper, 2.5), `angle?`, `leader?` |
| `spot` | EL | `at`, `view?`, `host?`: in a plan, the top of what stands there; in a section or an elevation, the point's height |
| `section` | CR | `start`, `end` (it looks to the left of the line), `depth?`, `name?` |
| `elevation` | | `facing?` (north, south, east or west: the side it shows), `at?`, or `start` and `end`; none of them: the four building elevations |
| `sheet` | | `number?` (A101, A102… by default), `name?`, `size?` (A0 to A4; A3 by default) |
| `place` | | `sheet` (its number), `view` (a level's, section's, elevation's, schedule's or 3D view's name: Room Schedule, `{3D}`…), `at?` (mm on the paper), `scale?` (100 for 1 : 100), `azimuth?` and `elevation?` for the 3D view |
| `delete_type` | | `category` and `type`, or `family`, or `family` and `type`: deletes a type of a category, a family, or one of a family's types; refused while an element uses it (it says how many) and for the last type of a category or of a family |
| `rename_type` | | `category` and `type`, or `family` and `type`, and `name`: renames a type of a category or one of a family's types; what's of it and what names it follow, and it keeps its GUID; refused for a name another type of it has |
| `purge` | PU | `kinds?` (`type`, `family`, `material`, `picture`, `filter`, `template`; types and families by default), `dry_run?`: takes out what nothing uses, again for what that frees; a category keeps a type and a family a type; `dry_run` lists what would go |

import zlib, struct, sys
def png(path, w, h, color):
    raw = b''.join(b'\x00' + bytes(color) * w for _ in range(h))
    def chunk(t, d):
        c = struct.pack('>I', len(d)) + t + d
        return c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(t + d) & 0xffffffff)
    data = b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' + chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', w, h, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) + chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b'IEND', b'')
    open(path, 'wb').write(data)

Off a category, that category's elements lose their values of it; deleted, every element does; renamed, they follow it. `inspect` lists them"
}
{

 "id": "modify",
 "label": "Modify",
 "menu": null,
 "params": "{id | ids: [id,…], …fields} change fields as `elements` shows them, of one element or several; `level` and `top_level` may be names. A filled region's or a floor's model pattern is set by `pattern_origin` [x, y], plan mm, where its lines start, and `pattern_angle`, degrees counter-clockwise (both shown by `elements`); to put a pattern line of one on a reference line, Model::align_pattern gives the `pattern_origin` that does. A floor's, a ceiling's, a roof's or a shaft's outline it sets is held to what `floor` says of it"
}

Its `texture` is what its surfaces look like in the 3D view, over its colour, a tile of it `size` mm across and up, turned `angle` degrees and moved `offset` mm: a pattern drawn in code, `kind` brick, block, boards, concrete, plaster, tile, roof, fabric, metal or insulation (at its natural size unless `size` says); or `image`, a picture: the PNG or JPEG file at `path`, taken into the project (up to 1024 px a side, 24 pictures), or one the project holds (`image`, its id from `inspect`); null takes the texture away
 `inspect` lists the library and the pictures
{action?: list|save|load|delete, kind?: material|family, name?, as?, replace?, path?} the user's favorites, kept in a file of their own (`path`; by default in their configuration folder) for every project to use: `save` the project's material or family `name` (a material with the picture its texture is made of, a family with the materials it is made of), under another name with `as`; `load` a favorite into the project, under another name with `as`, or over one it has already with `replace`; `delete` one from the favorites; `list` them (the default)
{kinds?: [type|family|material|picture|filter|template, …], dry_run?} takes out what nothing uses, again for what that leaves unused: types and families unless `kinds` says; a category keeps a type and a family a type; with `dry_run` it lists what would go and changes nothing
 `lens` is the focal length it is seen through, 10 to 600 mm on a 35 mm camera (whose 36 mm of film is the picture's width): 35 unless given or set before; turned off, it keeps it
 The eye stands back from the middle of the picture as far as the lens and the zoom say; `render` takes how high it stands
{kind?, name?} the project's library with its ids and GUIDs, as elements have them: each type (`kind` `type:wall`, `type:door`, `type:beam`…), material, picture, family, parameter, view filter and template (`view-filter`, `view-template`), phase, phase filter, design option set and design option (`option-set`, `design-option`, named `set: option`), family type and family parameter (`family-type`, `family-parameter`, named `family: name`); and `parts`, what entries hold that has its own id and GUID: each type's layers and each family's forms and symbols (`kind` `layer`, `form`, `symbol`; `name` the type's or the family's)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""batch.py cases.txt [-v]: each line 'fixture|cmd ;; cmd ...' (fixture a path; '-' for none);
runs cmp.py on `run in.bimcraft --cmd ... --save out.bimcraft` and prints SAME/DIFF per line."""
import os, subprocess, sys
MINE = '/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-a408f9f6869b9e8e8/target/release/bimcraft-cli'
verbose = '-v' in sys.argv
args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if a != '-v']
lines = [l.rstrip('\n') for l in open(args[0]) if l.strip() and not l.startswith('#')]
env = dict(os.environ, MINE=MINE)
nd = 0
for l in lines:
    fx, cmds = l.split('|', 1)
    fx = fx.strip()
    cl = []
    files = []
    for f in ('red.png', 'green.png', 'blue.png'):
        files += ['-f', '/tmp/edit-library/' + f]
    run = ['run']
    if fx != '-':
        files += ['-f', fx]
        run.append(os.path.basename(fx))
    for c in cmds.split(' ;; '):
        run += ['--cmd', c.strip()]
    run += ['--save', 'out.bimcraft']
    p = subprocess.run(['python3', '/tmp/tools/cmp.py'] + files + ['--'] + run, capture_output=True, text=True, env=env)
    res = p.stdout.strip().splitlines()
    ok = res and res[-1] == 'SAME'
    if not ok:
        nd += 1
    print(('SAME ' if ok else 'DIFF ') + l[:250])
    if not ok and verbose:
        for x in res[:-1][:40]:
            print('     ' + x[:250])
print('DIFFS', nd, 'of', len(lines))

All four commands are done and committed. Every case I compared with `cmp.py` matches the original exactly: replies, error texts, saved files and undo labels.

**Branch** `worktree-agent-a408f9f6869b9e8e8`, last commit `7409dc1`. The work is in `src/edit/purge.rs`, `types.rs`, `matchprops.rs`, a new `library_util.rs`, and in `mod.rs` I added the `pub mod` line and put `delete_type` and `match_properties` in `always_step`.

**Testing.** About 280 hand-written cases went through `cmp.py`, with saved files compared:
- Fixtures: a new project, a Portuguese one, the `--sample` house, the `--highrise` tower, an IFC round-trip, your `all.bimcraft`, a dozen I built for specific situations, and 40 random projects made with the original.
- Error texts were checked separately in about 650 single-command runs.
- On top of that, 1,450 random command sequences (purge, delete_type, rename_type, match_properties, plus undo) all came out the same.

**`purge`**
- Works in rounds. Each round lists what's unused at its start, in this order, each sorted by name: category types, families, family types, materials, pictures, view filters, view templates. It removes them all, then repeats until a round finds nothing.
- What counts as a use:
  - types and families: elements;
  - materials: the `types` and `families` sections, and paint;
  - pictures: materials' textures;
  - filters: views' graphics and templates;
  - templates: views' graphics.
- A category with no used type keeps its default type: the starter project's type by name if it still exists, else its first by name. A family with no used type keeps its last type by name.
- An emptied `images`, `view_filters` or `view_templates` section is removed; `families` stays as `{}`.
- Nothing removed means no undo step.
- One quirk: a material set only as a component's own parameter value isn't counted as used. The real purge is then refused by the original's model check ("component N: material `X` isn't in the library; add it with `material`"), while `dry_run` still lists it. I reproduce that check inside purge.

**`delete_type`**
- Category names are normalised: case, spaces, `_` and trailing s's are ignored, with special cases for masses, switches and pipe accessories.
- The "is used N times" check comes before the "last type" check.
- Deleting a family also removes its type and parameter library entries.
- Quirk: `text`, `dimension` and `region` are accepted. The original replies "deleted" but changes nothing, and still records an undo step. I copy that, which is why `delete_type` always records a step.

**`rename_type`**
- Keys are re-sorted after a rename and the GUID is kept. Elements don't change because they point at GUIDs, and filters and schedules naming the type don't follow it.
- Renaming to the same name records no step. For a family type, that reply's `from` is `Bed: 900 x 2000` rather than the plain type name.
- `family` without `type` never renames anything: it answers same-name, "already a family", or "there is no family `Bed`".
- A GUID-like name gets the model-check error, which I emulate.

**`match_properties`**
- Copies `type`. When `from` has a family it copies that too, inserting `family` right after `type` on doors and windows.
- On a family change, the element's own parameter values are re-keyed to the new family's parameters. Any the new family lacks are left under their plain name, and the existing parameters check then refuses them, as the original does.
- It always records an undo step.
- A family door given a project door type fails with "door N: type `X` doesn't exist (there are: …)"; I emulate that.

**What doesn't match, and what other areas must provide**
1. **Your `common::resolve`** (it affects delete, modify, move, etc.). The original refuses a library entry's GUID by its name (`"Generic - 200mm" is not an element id or GUID`) and an unknown GUID as `no element <guid>`. I used a local fix, `library_util::resolve_element` / `element_ids`, which you can move into `common.rs`.
2. **Global model check that `type:*` library names aren't GUIDs** ("wall type `…`: a name isn't a GUID; name it otherwise"). The `type` command needs it. `styles::common::check_library_names` skips `type:` kinds, and family types are exempt.
3. **ARCH: door and window checks.**
   - A family door or window must have one of its family's types.
   - It must still fit its wall after a type change, e.g. "window N: 1200 mm wide at offset 500 doesn't fit wall M, 1000 mm long".
   - I only cover the type-in-family check, for elements match_properties changes; the fit checks aren't emulated, so a match_properties that should fail on fit currently succeeds until ARCH adds them.
4. **The commands that place elements** can reuse `library_util::default_type`. It matched for wall, door and pipe; the default type of a component's family is its first type by name.
5. **Error clipping applies to every command's errors**: past 2,000 characters the original cuts and appends "… (N more characters)", counting characters. `library_util::clip_error` does it.

Fixtures and scripts are in `/tmp/edit-library/`; `fuzz.py` and `batch.py` re-run the comparisons.
